notes: This is the estate-wide shape behind OS-2/OS-4 and behind eight of the eleven Companion menu invariants: two things owning or describing one thing, and the stale one winning.

Overlaps `inv.engineering.036` ("one authoritative location per concern"), which is already canonical. Recorded here as the READ-PATH specialisation of it; if the operator judges it fully covered by 036, this candidate should be retired rather than ratified — a duplicate invariant is the defect 036 names.

canaries.assertion: 'one screen, one answer about whether registration happened' — the ladder tokenId falls back through card → receipt → this session's own confirmation, and a confirmed tokenId is never cleared by a later poll that fails to see it.
Projection-wins, receipt-fallback and chain-decode paths each assert their own `fallbackSource`, so which reader answered is always recoverable.

statement: One canonical reader owns the lookup of a fact; a consumer that re-implements the query becomes a second observer that will eventually disagree.

occurrences.defect: The route hand-built its own persona-keyed receipt query instead of consuming the canonical receipt reader, so it disagreed with the Evidence-receipts drawer about the same receipts on the same screen.

Two independent Supabase writes with nothing making them one transaction, and readers depending on both landing. The remedy was ONE resilient reader with a named `fallbackSource`, so a stuck write stays diagnosable rather than silently worked around forever.

sections (rendered text), carried (refs) and the omission Set were each computed from their OWN filter/map expression over the same underlying membership decision, rather than one canonical computation projected three ways. A mutation that changed which members were rendered left `carried` reporting the pre-mutation membership, so a canary asserting only on `carried` passed against code whose rendered output had genuinely changed. Fixed by deriving all three from one `membership` map.
